summary: Flaky: smoke DB-backed tests fail intermittently under load, a different test each run (commerce, inventory)
description:
Observed 2026-08-08 while gating **TKT-229**, on four consecutive `make check` runs. Each run failed
the **smoke** stage on a **different** DB-backed test, none of them related to the change under gate
(TypeScript only):

| Run | Failing test | Package |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `TestGroupReservationRepeatedDrawDownIsQuantityNeutral` | `inventory/internal/store` |
| 2 | `TestFullSeatedReturnReleasesEverySeat` | `inventory/internal/store` |
| 3 | `TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders` | `commerce/internal/store` |
| 4 (control, pristine `main`) | — smoke never reached; failed earlier at `test-ts` (the TKT-229 flake) | — |

**Not TKT-198 and not TKT-229.** Zero `already exists` / `partial migration` errors in every run, so
the migration race TKT-198 fixed is genuinely gone. TKT-229's diff is TypeScript only and cannot
reach a Go smoke test. The control run on pristine `main` confirms the TS flake is TKT-229's and is
fixed by it.

**A sample failure, and why it looks like ordering rather than logic:**

```
reservations_smoke_test.go:167: history[0].Action = draw_down, want reserve
```

The assertion wants `["reserve","draw_down","draw_down","draw_down"]` and got a draw_down first.
That is a **history ordering** claim. If `History()` orders by a timestamp with insufficient
resolution, rows written inside the same transaction — or the same millisecond — can tie, and the
tie-break is then whatever the database returns. Under load the writes bunch up and ties become
likely. **That is a hypothesis from one sample, not a diagnosis** — the other two failures were not
investigated and may be unrelated.

**Why it matters.** This is the third distinct load-sensitivity defect found in two days
(TKT-198 migration race, TKT-229 quadratic TS fixture, this). Each one makes `make check`
non-deterministic, and a gate that fails on machine load cannot certify anything — the same
blocking property that made TKT-198 urgent.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] The mechanism is identified for **each** observed failure, or the ones that turn out to share a
      cause are grouped with the evidence that says so.
- [ ] The failures reproduce deterministically before the fix, or the ticket says why not.
- [ ] No assertion is widened to pass. If `History()` really is ambiguously ordered, the fix is a
      total order in the query, not a laxer test.
- [ ] `make check` green three consecutive times **on a loaded machine**.

**Do not** fix by adding retries or by loosening the ordering assertions — an ordering guarantee the
tests stop checking is an ordering guarantee the code stops having.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed by **TKT-229**'s `agent:ai-review`/merge stage (gateless run, 2026-08-08) as an incidental. Not shaped — needs `shaping.md` before Gate 1. Evidence logs were at /tmp/g229_8.log, /tmp/g229_9.log, /tmp/gmain.log and /tmp/gctrl.log at the time of filing; the failing test names and the control-run result are transcribed above because those files are temporary.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### A fourth instance, on `main` after both fixes merged (2026-08-08)

A confirmation run of `make check` on `main` at `a0a596d` — TKT-198 and TKT-229 both merged — failed
the smoke stage on a **fourth distinct test**:

```
--- FAIL: TestMigrationsRanBeforeServicesStarted/payments
smoke_test.go:346: ticketing-smoke-0-payments-migrate-1 finished at 00:48:25.681558716,
but ticketing-smoke-0-payments-1 started at 00:48:25.162768220
— the service started before its migrations completed
```

**519 milliseconds.** Four of the five services passed; only `payments` inverted.

This strengthens the diagnosis: the failing tests share no code, but they all assert an **ordering or
timing relation with a small margin** — history row order, container start order. Under CPU
contention the margins close and the assertion flips. Zero `already exists` errors in this run, so
TKT-198's fix continues to hold.

**Note this one is about ADR-022's core guarantee** (`service_completed_successfully` gating), so the
right fix is probably to assert the *Compose dependency condition* rather than to compare wall-clock
timestamps — a test that measures a guarantee by timing can fail while the guarantee holds. That is a
hypothesis for the plan, not a decision.

**Running tally, all on unrelated code:** `TestGroupReservationRepeatedDrawDownIsQuantityNeutral`,
`TestFullSeatedReturnReleasesEverySeat`, `TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders`,
`TestMigrationsRanBeforeServicesStarted`. CI passes all of them on an unloaded runner.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Readiness verdict: **READY** (8/8 met) — scope narrowed, two failures split out

Shaped 2026-08-09 against `main` @ `4c995e8`. The `uncertainties` and `approach` items were
resolved **by measurement**, not by assumption, because the ticket's own COS forbids widening an
assertion to pass and that only makes sense once the mechanism is known.

#### The mechanism, proven

`claim_history` is read with `ORDER BY occurred_at, id` (`operational.go:336`, `capacity.go:131`).
`occurred_at` is `timestamptz DEFAULT now()`; `id` is `uuid.New()` — **UUIDv4, random, no time
component** (`store.go:102`). So the order is *total but not meaningful*: rows that tie on
`occurred_at` are ordered by a coin flip. That is why it survived review.

Measured against a real PostgreSQL (throwaway container, since torn down):

| Scenario | Rows | Distinct `occurred_at` | Collisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2000 inserts, one transaction | 2000 | 1 | 1999 |
| 300 inserts, separate transactions, serial | 300 | 300 | **0** |
| 1200 inserts, 8 concurrent writers, separate transactions | 1200 | 1199 | **1** |

The colliding pair was `{w4_35, w2_32}` — two *different* writers at
`2026-08-09 04:30:49.058874+00`, identical to the microsecond.

Serial → no collisions (passes on an idle machine). Concurrent → collisions appear (fails under
gate load). The observed `history[0].Action = draw_down, want reserve` is precisely a tie
resolved the wrong way. Note this is **not** the familiar "`now()` is transaction-start" intra-
transaction tie: `reserve` and each `draw_down` are written in *separate* transactions
(`reservations.go:132` and `:235`), and separate transactions still collide under concurrency.

#### Scope narrowed — and why

The ticket's COS says the mechanism must be identified for **each** observed failure. Two of the
four are **not** explained by the above and are being split out rather than carried:

- `TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders` (commerce) — uninvestigated.
- `TestMigrationsRanBeforeServicesStarted/payments` — a 519ms container-start inversion; a
  different assertion class entirely, and per the ticket's own note the right fix is probably to
  assert the Compose dependency condition rather than compare wall-clock timestamps.

Bundling unexplained failures into a ticket whose COS demands explained ones guarantees it cannot
close honestly. Also named as a deliberate exclusion: `access.lifecycle_events` uses the same
`ORDER BY occurred_at,id` shape (`migration_smoke_test.go:130`) and may share the latent
ambiguity — out of scope here, flagged so it is a choice and not an oversight.

#### Approach constraint the plan must solve

`claim_history` is append-only with a `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger
(`0003_operational_holds.sql:42-50`). The trigger does not fire on INSERT, but **any backfill of
existing rows is an UPDATE and is refused by the database**. Adding a `NOT NULL` monotonic column
to a table whose existing rows cannot be rewritten is the real design question — the in-repo
precedent is `bigserial` (`access/.../0003_lifecycle_integrity.sql:87,128`).

`risk:low` **not** claimed: this adds a data migration, which the label's own carve-outs exclude.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — and this run is **gateless by owner waiver**

**⚠ Waiver, recorded so the board history shows it.** The repo owner (Mathieu Dupuis) explicitly
waived **all four human gates** for this run as a deliberate process experiment, and directed the
agent to run `Ready → Done` continuously. Substitutions, as instructed:

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority | human moves Backlog → Ready | owner named the ticket; agent moved it |
| 2 — plan approval | human approves the plan | agent resolves open decisions itself, preferring the critique's recommendation; else the most reversible option. Every self-made decision recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |

| 4 — PO acceptance | PO validates COS | agent self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code |

Everything else in the skill applies unchanged: `config.models` routing with no substitutions,
cross-model review for both plan and code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check` green
before every push and after the merge, all marker comments, no AI attribution anywhere.

The `overrides:` list in the closing `kind=metrics` comment is the audit record for this waiver:
every point where a review pass raised a **blocking** objection and the agent proceeded anyway.

**Selection reason.** Owner-directed. Chosen over TKT-218 and TKT-149 — the two tickets originally
bundled into this run — because shaping proved those two are not implementable as written:
TKT-218's premise did not reproduce under 8 runs at load, and TKT-149 asks for a diagnostic that
has existed since TKT-82. Both were returned to the owner as decisions. TKT-230 is the only one of
the three with a proven defect, and it is actively making `make check` non-deterministic, which
blocks confident gating of every other ticket.

**Blockers:** none. TKT-198 and TKT-229 are merged; neither is implicated.

**Risk verdict: `risk:low` NOT claimed.** The work adds a **data migration** to an append-only
table — one of the label's four explicit carve-outs (auth, data migrations, CI/deploy config,
>5 files). Stating it explicitly per the skill's rule, even though the diff will be small: the
carve-out is exactly the case whose risk is obvious to the claimer and invisible in the thread
afterwards. The plan-review stage is therefore load-bearing here and is not skipped.

# TKT-230 execution plan

## 1. DoD

- `History` and `CapacityHistory` return a deterministic chronological order when `occurred_at` ties.
- New `claim_history` rows receive a database-assigned append sequence.
- Existing rows are not rewritten, and the append-only trigger remains enforced.
- The regression test fails on the current revision because UUID ordering reverses two same-timestamp rows, then passes after the change.
- No retries, widened assertions, or `-count=N`.
- Inventory has no remaining ordered `claim_history` reader using only `ORDER BY occurred_at, id`.
- `make check` passes three consecutive times on a loaded machine.

The current action vocabulary is:

`create`, `place`, `release`, `convert`, `finalize`, `confirm`, `expire`, `adjust_capacity`, `reserve`, `draw_down`, and `refund_return` (`services/inventory/internal/store/migrations/0010_refund_capacity_returns.sql:22-27`).

## 2. The design decision

Add a nullable `BIGINT append_order` to `claim_history`, backed by a PostgreSQL sequence and populated by a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger.

The read order becomes:

```sql
ORDER BY occurred_at, append_order NULLS FIRST, id
```

`occurred_at` remains the primary chronological key. `append_order` resolves timestamp ties for all rows created after the migration. `id` remains only as the final tie-breaker for legacy rows that have no append order.

### Migration shape

Create `0012_claim_history_append_order.sql`:

```sql
CREATE SEQUENCE claim_history_append_order_seq AS bigint;

ALTER TABLE claim_history
  ADD COLUMN append_order bigint
    CONSTRAINT claim_history_append_order_positive
    CHECK (append_order IS NULL OR append_order > 0);

ALTER SEQUENCE claim_history_append_order_seq
  OWNED BY claim_history.append_order;

ALTER TABLE claim_history
  ALTER COLUMN append_order
  SET DEFAULT nextval('claim_history_append_order_seq');

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX claim_history_append_order_uidx
  ON claim_history (append_order)
  WHERE append_order IS NOT NULL;
```

Add an insert trigger that assigns `nextval(...)` when an INSERT explicitly supplies `NULL`, so every future row receives an order value even if a new writer bypasses the default.

Replace the existing lookup indexes with ordered variants:

```sql
CREATE INDEX claim_history_claim
  ON claim_history (claim_id, occurred_at, append_order NULLS FIRST, id);

CREATE INDEX claim_history_pool
  ON claim_history (pool_id, occurred_at, append_order NULLS FIRST, id)
  WHERE pool_id IS NOT NULL;
```

Use plain `CREATE INDEX`, not `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, per `docs/adr/ADR-020-catalog-index-build-concurrency.md:80-115`.

The migration must not contain an `UPDATE claim_history`. The existing trigger rejects updates and deletes (`services/inventory/internal/store/migrations/0003_operational_holds.sql:41-50`), and ADR-023 explicitly defines the trail as append-only with no invented baseline rows (`docs/adr/ADR-023-operational-holds-and-conversion.md:56-62`).

Pre-existing rows remain `append_order IS NULL`. They cannot be assigned their true historical append position: the database has only `occurred_at` and a random UUID, and rewriting them would violate the trail contract. For legacy rows sharing a timestamp, `id` preserves the existing total-order fallback, but that order must be described as a stable legacy tie-break—not reconstructed chronology. New rows have a meaningful insertion-order tie-break.

### Rejected alternatives

- **Backfill a `NOT NULL` column with `UPDATE`.** Rejected because the append-only trigger refuses it, and the original append order is not recoverable.
- **Populate legacy rows from `(occurred_at, id)`.** Rejected because it would canonize the UUID coin flip as if it were historical truth.
- **Use only a higher-precision timestamp or `clock_timestamp()`.** Rejected because separate concurrent transactions can still receive equal timestamps, which is the observed failure.
- **Use UUID ordering as the permanent solution.** Rejected because `appendHistory` supplies UUIDv4 values with no time component (`services/inventory/internal/store/store.go:102-105`).
- **Add a companion order table.** This is technically viable and resembles the access-service integrity side table (`services/access/internal/store/migrations/0003_lifecycle_integrity.sql:18-34`), but it adds a join and a second coverage invariant. An inline nullable sequence plus an insert trigger solves new-row ordering without changing the immutable row shape; it still honestly leaves legacy chronology unresolved.

The migration remains embedded and owned by inventory. It will be applied by the inventory `migrate` job, not the server path (`docs/adr/ADR-022-out-of-band-service-migrations.md:101-111`; `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:64-80`).

## 3. Files to change

- `services/inventory/internal/store/migrations/0012_claim_history_append_order.sql`
  - Add the nullable append-order column, sequence, default, insert trigger, uniqueness constraint/indexes, and guarded down migration.
  - Do not rewrite existing `claim_history` rows.

- `services/inventory/internal/store/operational.go:331-349`
  - Change `History` from `ORDER BY occurred_at, id` to `ORDER BY occurred_at, append_order NULLS FIRST, id`.

- `services/inventory/internal/store/capacity.go:119-145`
  - Apply the same ordering to `CapacityHistory`.

- `services/inventory/internal/store/history_order_smoke_test.go` (new)
  - Add the deterministic timestamp-tie regression test.
  - Add migration/trigger assertions if the test harness can exercise the upgrade from migration 0011.

No writer SQL needs to change: `sweepExpired` (`services/inventory/internal/store/store.go:68-76`), `appendHistory` (`services/inventory/internal/store/store.go:102-105`), and capacity adjustment inserts (`services/inventory/internal/store/capacity.go:83-85`) all omit the new column and will use the database assignment trigger/default.

## 4. Test plan

### Deterministic pre-fix regression

Add a smoke test that:

1. Creates an inventory pool and fixture claim.
2. Begins one SQL transaction.
3. Reads one timestamp once, for example `SELECT now()`.
4. Inserts a `reserve` history row with a deliberately high UUID.
5. Inserts a `draw_down` history row with a deliberately low UUID.
6. Supplies the exact same timestamp to both INSERTs.
7. Commits and calls `st.History`.
8. Asserts the result is:

```text
reserve, draw_down
```

The current query at `services/inventory/internal/store/operational.go:335-336` sorts the low UUID first, so this test fails deterministically before the fix. It does not depend on load, scheduling, transaction-start timestamp behavior, retries, or repeated test runs. After the migration, the first INSERT receives the lower append sequence and the assertion passes.

The test should also assert both new rows have non-null, distinct append-order values.

### Existing tests that must remain green

- `TestGroupReservationRepeatedDrawDownIsQuantityNeutral` in `services/inventory/internal/store/reservations_smoke_test.go:84-173`
  - Verifies the exact `reserve`, `draw_down`, `draw_down`, `draw_down` order that currently flakes.
  - Also verifies child linkage, quantity neutrality, and idempotent replay.

- `TestGroupReservationPlacementExpiryAndAudit` in `services/inventory/internal/store/reservations_smoke_test.go:25-82`
  - Verifies `reserve` precedes the later `expire` audit event.

- `TestOperationalConvertIsQuantityNeutralAndAudited` in `services/inventory/internal/store/operational_smoke_test.go:135-211`
  - Verifies `place`, `convert`, `release` ordering and confirms UPDATE/DELETE remain rejected.

- `TestCapacityAdjustmentIdempotencyAndAudit` in `services/inventory/internal/store/capacity_adjustments_smoke_test.go:127-197`
  - Verifies ordered capacity audit records, immutable replay results, and append-only enforcement.

- Refund-return replay tests
  - `services/inventory/internal/store/refund_returns.go:88-101` reads a unique idempotency receipt by organizer and key, so it should remain unaffected by history presentation ordering.

Finally, run the loaded `make check` gate three consecutive times.

## 5. Risks

- **Legacy ambiguity remains bounded.** Rows written before migration cannot receive their true append position. Their same-timestamp order remains the old UUID fallback. The implementation must not claim to reconstruct chronology that the stored data cannot prove.

- **Sequence order is allocation order, not a gapless commit counter.** Rolled-back transactions may consume sequence values. That is acceptable because the requirement is a total order, not gaplessness. For the affected reservation paths, mutations are serialized under the pool lock (`docs/adr/ADR-027-group-agency-reservations.md:40-63`).

- **Replay semantics should not change.** ADR-027 stores staff keys in `claim_history` (`docs/adr/ADR-027-group-agency-reservations.md:64-67`), but the implementation resolves replays by the unique `(organizer_id, idempotency_key)` lookup (`services/inventory/internal/store/operational.go:82-99`). Changing `History` ordering must not change which immutable receipt is returned.

- **All INSERT paths must remain covered.** The sequence trigger should cover `appendHistory`, expiry-sweep inserts, capacity adjustments, refund returns, and direct SQL fixtures. A migration test should verify an explicit `NULL` append order is assigned rather than accepted.

- **Index migration duration.** Rebuilding the two inventory history indexes takes locks and remains subject to the 30-second migration deadline. ADR-022 makes this an out-of-band one-shot job, but it does not remove the deadline (`docs/adr/ADR-022-out-of-band-service-migrations.md:107-121`).

- **Out-of-scope reader.** The access service still has legacy `occurred_at,id` ordering paths, including `services/access/internal/store/postgres.go:228-237` and `services/access/internal/store/lifecycle_checkpoint.go:317`. It must not be changed under TKT-230; that is the deliberate TKT-231/TKT-232 exclusion.

- Other `claim_history` reads found are key-based lookups, existence checks, counts, or aggregates (`services/inventory/internal/store/operational.go:87-99`, `services/inventory/internal/store/refund_returns.go:94-101`, `services/inventory/internal/store/store.go:160-168`, `smoke/onsale_load_test.go:210-211`). They do not require chronological ordering.

## 6. What I could not verify

- I did not run PostgreSQL migrations or the new regression test.
- I did not reproduce the current failure against a live loaded database.
- I did not run `make check` three consecutive times.
- I did not measure the rebuilt index duration or inspect the resulting query plans.
- I did not verify the actual volume or distribution of pre-existing `claim_history` rows in a deployed database.

objective.note: make check is non-deterministic: DB-backed smoke tests fail under machine load, a different test each run. A gate that fails on load cannot certify anything. This ticket closes the ONE mechanism that has been proven; the other observed failures are split out (see scope).

scope.note: IN: claim_history ordering in inventory — the ORDER BY occurred_at, id pattern at operational.go:336 and capacity.go:131, and whatever total order replaces it. OUT, split to their own tickets because their mechanism is NOT established: TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders (commerce) and TestMigrationsRanBeforeServicesStarted/payments (a 519ms container-start inversion, a different assertion class). OUT: access.lifecycle_events, which uses the same ORDER BY occurred_at,id shape and may share the latent ambiguity — named here so it is a deliberate exclusion rather than an oversight.

uncertainties.note: RESOLVED at shaping by measurement against a real PostgreSQL. claim_history orders by (occurred_at, id): occurred_at is timestamptz DEFAULT now(), id is uuid.New() = UUIDv4, random, no time component. Measured: 300 inserts in separate serial transactions -> 300 distinct timestamps, 0 collisions. 1200 inserts across 8 CONCURRENT writers in separate transactions -> 1199 distinct, 1 collision ({w4_35, w2_32}, two different writers, identical to the microsecond). A tie is then broken by a random UUID, so History() returns an arbitrary order. That is exactly the observed 'history[0].Action = draw_down, want reserve'. Serial passes, concurrent fails: the idle/loaded split the flake reports. NOTE the order is already TOTAL but not MEANINGFUL, which is why it survived review.

dependencies.note: None open. TKT-198 (migration race) and TKT-229 (quadratic TS fixture) are merged; neither is implicated — zero 'already exists' errors in every observed run.

approach.note: Give claim_history a monotonic tie-break and order by it. Precedent in-repo: access lifecycle_event_integrity.sequence and lifecycle_checkpoints.checkpoint_id are bigserial for exactly this reason (0003_lifecycle_integrity.sql:87,128). Constraint from ADR-003/ADR-023: claim_history is append-only and carries a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger (0003_operational_holds.sql:42-50) — the trigger does not fire on INSERT, but any backfill of existing rows would be an UPDATE and is therefore refused by construction. A new NOT NULL column with a sequence default on a table whose existing rows must not be rewritten is the actual design question for the plan. COS forbids widening the assertion instead.

first_slice.note: One slice, one PR: migration adding the monotonic column + switch both ORDER BY sites + a test that FAILS on the current code. The test must force the tie deterministically (insert two history rows with an identical occurred_at and assert the returned order), not rely on -count=N or on load — same discipline as TKT-132/134.

success.note: COS already on the ticket, narrowed to the in-scope half: (1) mechanism identified for the inventory history failures — done at shaping, evidence above; (2) the failure reproduces deterministically before the fix; (3) no assertion widened — a total order in the query, not a laxer test; (4) make check green three consecutive times on a loaded machine.

context_memo.note: Baked below at shaping time, governingAdrs resolved against docs/adr/ at HEAD 4c995e8.

governingAdrs.why: claim_history is one of the append-only trails. Its ordering is a RECONSTRUCTION guarantee — 'any ticket's authoritative history is reconstructible from its trace' — so an ambiguous order is a defect against this ADR, not merely a flaky test. It also forbids fixing the flake by rewriting or reordering existing rows.

Defines claim_history as append-only with action/actor/reason/quantities per mutation, and puts staff idempotency keys in it under a unique partial index. The append-only trigger it introduced (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE) means a backfill of a new ordering column on existing rows is refused by the database.

Group reservations register staff keys in claim_history with actions reserve/draw_down — the exact rows whose order the failing assertion checks. Its staff-op shape is 'pool lock -> claim_history registry replay -> ...', so history order participates in idempotency replay, not just in reporting.
Migrations run out-of-band via each binary's migrate subcommand as a one-shot Compose job. A new inventory migration must work under that path; the server path never migrates.
Still governs everything ADR-022 did not supersede: goose-as-library, embedded SQL, per-service ownership, fail-fast, 30s bound. The new migration is inventory's.

reference.summary: Failing assertion: reservations_smoke_test.go:167, wants [reserve, draw_down x3]
Ordering sites to change: operational.go:336 and capacity.go:131
appendHistory supplies uuid.New() (UUIDv4) as the tie-break
In-repo bigserial precedent for an append-only trail's order
